sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r7/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 3 (#2 instruction_preserves_natural_human_voice); Internal Quality Checks row 3 (no annotations/comments on the row); Deterministic Checks row 13 (check-instruction-content.py leaves voice to the rubric)
evidence: Read instruction.md and all three notes in full against workbook row #2 and quality-checks.md:13-15 (verify sentence variety, contractions, occasional terse fragment; defect = uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, or voice shift between brief and notes). Voice is a consistent first-person firm owner throughout (we/our/us, plus I in conversations.md:'When I open a matter', 'a half-typed reply, where I've scrolled to'), with concrete situational colour: instruction.md:1 'our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last'; conversations.md 'Our internet in court is patchy', 'Clients paste all sorts into chat', 'People fix typos and figures'; walls-and-retention.md 'a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us', 'Conflicts come up mid-matter'. Contractions are frequent across every file (grep: doesn't x3, can't x4, don't x2, mustn't, isn't, won't, aren't, I'm, I've). Sentence length varies from short ('Dev Anand is walled from M-12 today.', 'Everyone signs in with password123.', 'Deleting can't be undone, so the app asks us to confirm first...') to longer explanatory sentences. Grep for LLM/marketing tells (seamless, robust, delve, leverage, ensure, comprehensive, intuitive, streamline, utilize, furthermore, moreover, additionally, crucial, em dashes, shall) found none; 'must' appears only 4 times in natural phrasing ('Two things matter more than anything else'). No bullet lists; the only table is the accounts table in walls-and-retention.md, which is a natural way for a person to list logins. Template controls nothing here (template instruction.md/notes.md are CHANGE_ME placeholders), and the template integration.md's impersonal spec voice was rewritten into the firm's voice ('We start the app with Node 22...'), so no voice shift between brief and notes. Counter-checks: a plausible LLM-polished brief that would wrongly pass would show uniform parallel bullets and gloss words; none present. A conforming alternative that could fail: the notes repeatedly open sections with a 'reason, so rule' pattern (Replies, Edits, Formatting, walls) and contain a few test-shaped sentences ('Typing the words "On hold" into a message mustn't make it look held'); I judge this a mild stylistic regularity that still reads as a person explaining their firm's needs, not robotic prose, so non-blocking for this row (spec-density belongs to row 1/6, not voice). Not a measured or portal result; this is a manual reading judgment.
